title: Foxtrail Systems Onboarding Kickstart
summary: Initial onboarding kickstart to align implementation scope, network and security prerequisites, pilot plan and success metrics. AE + CSM + SE from Redwood joined customer platform and security stakeholders to confirm timeline and next steps for a dedicated pilot in Q1.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-22
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Park (CSM), Lena Ortiz (SE) — Foxtrail: Rajiv, Sofia, Tom, Priya

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE for Foxtrail. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Rajiv Malhotra: Rajiv here, hi.
[00:09] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia — platform team.
[00:11] Tom Brenner: Tom on security.
[00:12] Priya Singh: Priya from product.
[00:14] Devon Park: Devon, customer success.
[00:16] Lena Ortiz: Lena, solutions engineering.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Cool. Agenda is lightweight — security needs, network peering, pilot scope and success metrics, and timeline. We want to leave with clear next steps.

[02:04] Rajiv Malhotra: To frame this — we're replacing a homegrown embedding service and want lower token cost for chat features. Main constraints: latency under 200ms p50 for short prompts, and data cannot leave EU for certain datasets. Also need audit logs.

[03:15] Maya Chen: Got it. For latency, are you targeting user-facing chat or async batch?

[03:22] Priya Singh: User-facing, so latency matters. Some requests are long — like multi-turn resumes — but most are sub-200 tokens.

[04:10] Lena Ortiz: Two quick notes — we can suggest model variant/quantization to meet cost; also prefix/KV cache will help for multi-turn continuity. For EU residency, we have region pinning and private deployments.

[05:30] Tom Brenner: On the security side, we need SOC 2 + encryption at rest with our KMS. Also SAML SSO and RBAC. How do you integrate with customer-managed KMS?

[05:48] Maya Chen: We support customer KMS via our private deployment and KMS integrations; for hosted accounts we use envelope encryption but can set up customer-managed keys for Private. I'll send our security packet after the call.

[07:20] Tom Brenner: And audit logs? We need token-level logging and ability to export to our SIEM for 90 days.

[07:33] Devon Park: We do have trace-level logs and configurable retention. For Private deployments we can forward logs to your CloudWatch or Splunk. We'll include specifics in the packet.

[09:02] Sofia Alvarez: Networking — can you do VPC peering to our AWS account or do you require a connector?

[09:15] Lena Ortiz: Two options: VPC peering to Redwood Dedicated nodes in your region, or set up a private deployment in your VPC via our on-prem package. For a pilot, most customers start with VPC peering into dedicated pool.

[10:03] Rajiv Malhotra: How long does it take to spin up dedicated capacity? We might want it for a 4-week pilot starting early Feb.

[10:12] Maya Chen: Typical lead time is 5–10 business days once we have CIDR, peering contact, and contractual addendum. For Q1 pilot we should start networking this week.

[12:11] Priya Singh: Success criteria — we want 95th percentile latency under 400ms and cost per 1k tokens under $X (we'll fill exact number in doc). Also stability >99% for pilot. Is that realistic?

[12:32] Lena Ortiz: Those are reasonable targets for a dedicated pool with caching and quantized model. We'll provide a recommended config and a benchmark script.

[14:05] Tom Brenner: About data retention — some datasets are PII. Does Redwood provide path-based redaction or configurable retention?

[14:18] Devon Park: For Private we can disable retention, and hosted has configurable retention windows; we also have eval hooks to exclude sensitive inputs. We'll include configuration options.

[15:40] Rajiv Malhotra: Any known limitations with long context windows? Our use-case sometimes needs 8k context.

[15:52] Lena Ortiz: We support models up to 32k depending on variant; for cost/latency tradeoffs we often recommend 8–16k for production. We can run a focused perf test on your long-context prompts.

[17:30] Priya Singh: Onboarding plan — what's the typical playbook?

[17:40] Devon Park: Week 0: network + security handshakes, Week 1: provisioning + smoke tests, Weeks 2–3: benchmarks and integration, Week 4: evaluation & decision. We usually run weekly syncs.

[19:05] Maya Chen: We'll assign a sandbox API key for the integration tests; this key will be rate-limited to match your expected pilot throughput.

[19:42] Rajiv Malhotra: Can you send a sample load script? We use JMeter but can adapt.

[19:54] Lena Ortiz: Yes, I'll upload a sample JMeter and a small python load generator to the shared drive.

[21:10] Tom Brenner: Compliance doc — can you provide SOC 2 Type II report extracts and your penetration test cadence?

[21:26] Maya Chen: Yes, SOC 2 summary and penetration test overview will be included. If you need full reports we can share under an NDA.

[22:55] Sofia Alvarez: For SSO, we use Okta. What SAML flows are supported?

[23:05] Devon Park: We support SAML 2.0 with SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, SCIM provisioning optional. We'll add SAML config docs to the packet.

[24:50] Priya Singh: Rate limits — we have peak concurrent users ~500, average 120 rps. What throttles should we expect?

[25:04] Lena Ortiz: For Dedicated we can set burst and sustained rates to meet those numbers; we'll need your expected token size distribution to recommend instance sizing.

[26:40] Rajiv Malhotra: Also hoping for quick rollback strategies if we see quality regressions when changing models.

[26:52] Maya Chen: We support version pinning and can route a percentage of traffic to a canary model. If quality drops we can auto-fallback to a baseline model. We'll show you an example rollout policy.

[28:11] Tom Brenner: Are there any temporary logs or caching that might retain PII? We need guarantees on deletion.

[28:25] Devon Park: For Private we can configure no persistent logs in service; for hosted we have retention policies and deletion workflows. We'll document exact data flows.

[30:00] Priya Singh: Timeline recap — we want pilot kickoff week of Feb 2, run 4 weeks. Does that align?

[30:10] Maya Chen: Yes, if we get peering info this week we can provision before Feb 2.

[31:50] Rajiv Malhotra: Customer-side owners: Rajiv will own ML requirements, Sofia handles infra peering, Tom owns security/compliance, Priya is PM.

[33:00] Maya Chen: Great — Redwood contacts: Maya AE (commercial), Devon CSM (success cadence), Lena SE (benchmarks & runbooks).

[34:15] Lena Ortiz: Quick demo note — we suggest running two benchmark types: short-chat steady state and long-context regen to validate KV cache benefits.

[35:40] Sofia Alvarez: For the peering we need a maintenance window; our infra team prefers 02:00–04:00 UTC. Can you accommodate?

[35:55] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll schedule peering during that window with our infra ops.

[36:40] Tom Brenner: A few follow-ups on legal — data processing addendum, subprocessor list. How do we get those?

[36:51] Maya Chen: I'll share the DPA and subprocessor list; legal can engage if you need modifications.

[38:15] Rajiv Malhotra: Anything we should be aware of for embeddings — vector dimension, similarity algo?

[38:28] Lena Ortiz: We'll recommend vector size and model family based on your dataset and retrieval recall targets. We'll include embedding recommendations in the runbook.

[40:02] Priya Singh: Can we get a sample SLA for Dedicated pilot?

[40:10] Devon Park: For pilots we provide best-effort targets; production Dedicated includes SLA options. We'll share a pilot-level SLA doc.

[41:30] Maya Chen: I'll send links to the security packet, SAML setup doc, and the benchmark runbook. Lena will post sample scripts. Devon will schedule the weekly syncs starting first week after provisioning.

[43:05] Rajiv Malhotra: One more question: do you support customer-hosted model versions if we want to use an internally validated model?

[43:17] Lena Ortiz: For Private deployments we can ingest customer model artifacts; for Hosted we can bring model weights under partnership — both require validation slides and sizing. We'll detail requirements.

[45:00] Priya Singh: Ok that sounds good. Let's recap the immediate asks.

[45:08] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to send security packet (Maya), benchmark runbook + scripts (Lena), schedule pilot kickoff week of Feb 2 (Devon). Foxtrail to provide CIDR and peering contact (Sofia), confirm success metric numbers (Priya/Rajiv).

[46:20] Tom Brenner: We'll review the security packet and follow up with any legal questions.

[46:45] Rajiv Malhotra: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the pilot.

[46:52] Maya Chen: Thanks team — we'll follow up with the links and invites.

End of transcript.
